mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending may decline.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises by >0.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in the subsequent 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in unemployment and decreases in payroll employment indicate a weakening labor market, which may negatively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases but S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests reduced economic output, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings could be affected.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines by >1% but S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% but S&P 500 returns are positive in the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates reduced consumer demand in the housing market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as related industries are impacted.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines by >5% but S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 5-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP growth indicates reduced economic activity, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate revenues and earnings are affected.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines by >1% but S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 days.
